questions.question: A service handles 1 billion requests per day with a 3x peak factor. What peak request rate should the first capacity estimate use?
options: About 3,000 requests/s
About 11,600 requests/s
About 35,000 requests/s
About 1 million requests/s
questions.explanation: One billion divided by 86,400 is about 11,600 requests/s on average; multiplying by three gives roughly 34,800 requests/s at peak.

questions.question: Why should conversation, web text, and document translation use separate serving routes?
options: They have different deadlines, sequence lengths, quality needs, and failure costs.
Each workload requires a separate user database.
Document translation never uses machine learning.
A shared model cannot support more than one content type.
questions.explanation: The workloads can share model infrastructure, but their latency budgets, batching behavior, quality policies, and degraded modes differ.

questions.question: Which cache key is safest for an eligible repeated translation?
options: Source text only
Target language only
User ID and current timestamp
Normalized source plus language direction, model, glossary, policy, and normalization versions
questions.explanation: Translation output changes with direction, model, terminology, policy, and normalization. The key must encode those boundaries, and the content must be eligible for retention.

questions.question: When is pivot translation through an intermediate language a defensible fallback?
options: Whenever it is cheaper, without separate evaluation
For a sparse direct pair when the pivot route has its own quality, latency, and disclosure policy
For every high-resource pair because two models are always more accurate
Only when the source and target languages are identical
questions.explanation: A pivot can extend coverage, but it adds another latency and semantic-loss boundary. It must be evaluated and surfaced as a distinct route.

questions.question: A medical translation clears the model confidence threshold. What should authorize automatic release?
options: The confidence score alone
A high global BLEU average
The domain release policy, including specialist review where required
The fact that the sentence is short
questions.explanation: Modeled confidence does not replace domain authority. Consequential content follows explicit policy and specialist review requirements.

questions.question: Which evaluation result is most useful before launching a new language direction?
options: One aggregate quality score across all languages
Only the average inference cost
Only fluent examples selected by the model team
Slice results for that direction, dialect, domain, entities, numbers, negation, latency, and fallback behavior
questions.explanation: Aggregate quality can hide severe local failures. Launch evidence must cover the actual language direction and its important correctness and serving slices.
